# bit-context v0.2.0

This release hardens session storage and adds an independently installable Codex skill.

## Breaking behavior

- The compatibility wrapper now requires an explicit `BITCTX_SESSION`; it no longer falls back to `default`.
- `set` no longer creates an uninitialized session. Run `init` first.
- Session IDs are restricted to a safe single path component.

## New behavior

- Select an isolated store with `--data-dir <PATH>` or `BITCTX_DATA_DIR`. Precedence is CLI option, environment variable, then `~/.bitctx`.
- `init` writes a zeroed `session.json`, so a new session can be evaluated immediately.
- `eval` retains `missing` and `missing_labels` and adds ordered `missing_conditions` objects.
- Per-session shared and exclusive locks, atomic synced writes, and private Unix permissions improve state safety.
- `bit-context-skill.zip` contains the Codex `SKILL.md`, discovery metadata, wrapper, and example schema.

## Compatibility and support boundary

- Valid v0.1 `schema.json` and `session.json` files remain readable with the same schema hash algorithm.
- Release binaries support Linux and macOS on x86-64 and ARM64.
- Windows is not supported in v0.2.0.
- Session state remains plaintext JSON and must not contain secrets.
